title: Embryologist Salary Australia: Converting Hourly Rates to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert an embryologist salary Australia hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and after-tax figures using the 38-hour week, award rates, and tax brackets.
salarySummary: For a full-time embryologist working 38 hours per week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52, with super paid on top.

faqs.q: What is the current National Minimum Wage in Australia?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour.

faqs.q: How do I find the correct award rate for an embryologist?
faqs.a: Embryologists are often covered by the Health Professionals and Support Services Award 2020. The Fair Work Commission’s Modern Awards Pay Database provides the official minimum rates, allowances, and penalty rates. Always check the specific award classification for your role.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the hourly rate or paid on top?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The current Super Guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. It is not deducted from your hourly rate.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Annual Pay Formula

When you have an hourly rate, the simplest way to estimate your annual gross pay is to multiply that rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. Most full-time roles in Australia are based on a 38-hour week, so the formula becomes:

**Annual gross pay ≈ hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, if you earn $40 per hour, your annual gross pay would be approximately $40 × 38 × 52 = $79,040. This calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It is a starting point for budgeting and comparing job offers.

Knowing your fortnightly pay is also useful. Simply multiply your weekly pay by two. Using the same $40 per hour example, weekly pay is $1,520, so fortnightly pay is $3,040 before tax and super.

## The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

Australia’s National Minimum Wage is the legal floor for award/agreement-free employees. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week for 38 hours, as confirmed by the Fair Work Commission. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, bringing the casual minimum to $33.05 per hour.

Most employees, including embryologists, are covered by a modern award that sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Commission’s Modern Awards Pay Database is the authoritative source for these rates. For health professionals, the Health Professionals and Support Services Award 2020 often applies. The database includes classifications, wage-related allowances, and penalty rates updated after each Annual Wage Review. Always check the specific classification that matches your role and experience level.

## Embryologist Salary Australia: Where to Find Reliable Rates

If you are researching an embryologist salary Australia, the most reliable figures come from official sources, not recruiter surveys. The Fair Work Ombudsman’s Pay and Conditions Tool (P.A.C.T.) can help you find the correct award and minimum pay for your job. The Australian Bureau of Statistics also publishes Average Weekly Earnings, which for full-time adult ordinary time was $2,083.70 per week in May 2026. This figure includes all industries and gives a broader benchmark, but it may not reflect the specific award rate for embryologists.

Because embryologists work in fertility clinics and hospitals, their pay may also include allowances for on-call work, shift penalties, or weekend work. The Modern Awards Pay Database includes these extras, but the simple hourly-to-annual conversion does not account for them. For a precise estimate, you should combine the base award rate with any applicable loadings from the database.

## Tax and Medicare on Your Annual Salary

Once you have your annual gross pay, you can estimate your take-home pay using the 2026–27 resident tax rates. The tax-free threshold is $18,200. Above that, you pay:

- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

In addition, most residents pay the Medicare levy of 2% of taxable income. The Medicare levy reduction thresholds for singles (used here) are based on the 2025–26 figures, as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this estimate. If your income is below the threshold, the levy may be reduced or eliminated.

For example, on a gross annual salary of $79,040, your taxable income after the $18,200 threshold is $60,840. The tax would be approximately $5,092 (15% on $26,800) plus $4,752 (30% on $15,840) = $9,844, plus Medicare levy of $1,580.80, giving total tax of about $11,425. Your after-tax annual pay would be roughly $67,615.

## Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation is not deducted from your hourly rate or your gross pay. The Super Guarantee requires your employer to contribute an additional 12% of your ordinary time earnings into a super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. This means if your annual gross pay is $79,040, your employer would contribute an extra $9,484.80 to your super, making your total employment cost $88,524.80.

When comparing job offers, remember that super is on top of your salary, not part of it. The [the timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate and see the annual figure with super added separately.

## Casual Loading and Fortnightly Pay

If you work casually, your hourly rate should include a 25% loading as compensation for not receiving paid leave. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how this works. When using the timesheet, you check a box to add the 25% loading on top of your base rate. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

Fortnightly pay is common in many industries. To calculate it, multiply your weekly gross pay by two. For a casual embryologist earning $33.05 per hour (base $26.44 plus loading), weekly pay for 38 hours is $1,255.90, so fortnightly pay is $2,511.80 before tax.

## Putting It All Together: Example

Let’s say you are an embryologist covered by the Health Professionals and Support Services Award 2020, and your classification rate is $40 per hour. You work 38 hours per week, full-time.

- Annual gross: $40 × 38 × 52 = $79,040
- Fortnightly gross: $79,040 ÷ 26 = $3,040
- Super (12% on top): $9,484.80
- Estimated tax and Medicare: ~$11,425
- Annual after-tax: ~$67,615

This estimate does not include any penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. For a more personalised calculation, refer to the [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data) available on this site.

Remember, the Fair Work Commission and Fair Work Ombudsman are the definitive sources for minimum pay. Always check the Modern Awards Pay Database or use the P.A.C.T. tool to confirm your correct award rate.
